### Day 357: Revelation 14:1–5
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-357-revelation-14-15.html
Passage: Revelation 14:3
Points:
- Praise songs gain deep personal meaning when sung through our own experiences of suffering and deliverance.
- The new song of the 144,000 represents a distinct quality arising from their unique redeemed lives.
- God places fresh spiritual songs of hope and truth into hearts that endure difficult wilderness seasons.
- Songs of the heart cannot be learned secondhand; they must be forged through personal faith.
- Pain and hardships handed over to Jesus are redeemed into lasting victories that cannot be stolen.

### A Song of Victory
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/a-song-of-victory
Passage: Revelation 14:2–3
Points:
- The seal of God marks believers with His name, guaranteeing true divine security and protection.
- The 144,000 represent God's faithful people standing firm as holy soldiers against evil.
- The new song echoes biblical victory songs sung after triumph in battle.
- Believers sing in celebration because the Lamb has decisively conquered sin and darkness.
- Gathering for Christian worship is a joyful response to the victory Christ won by grace.
